messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 15 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QBR prep: ACME health snapshot + renewal risk & exec asks

Team — kicking off the QBR prep thread for Acme (renewal Q3). I pulled the attached health snapshot and a short renewal risk register; please review and add your items by EOD Friday. High-level summary up front: 

- Current renewal status: Negotiation stage. Procurement has requested MAA language; legal review in progress.
- Health score: 71/100 (decline from 82 over last quarter). Primary drivers: two incidents in Jan with elevated token loss windows, and slow adoption of the new streaming SDK in the ML infra team.
- Support incidence: Sev2 on 2028-01-28 (KV-caching mismatch) — mitigated but customer noted SLA concerns.
- Usage trend: steady query growth +12% QoQ, but average latency for long-context dev endpoints is +35ms vs our SLO.

Please do the following in the shared drive doc linked below: 
1) Add top 3 technical risks (one-liners) into the Risk Register tab.
2) For each risk add: owner (internal), mitigation plan, and an estimated impact to renewal (Low/Med/High).
3) Propose up to two exec attention items we should surface to the Redwood leadership briefing (one-sentence each).

Attachments: ACME_QBR_health_snapshot_20280215.xlsx (customer metrics & incident timeline), MAA_draft_ACME_v1.2.pdf (draft Master Agreement with proposed opt-outs).
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AcmeQBRPrep
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/ACME-42

Target: consolidate and send an exec one-pager by Monday 20 Feb for Friday 24 Feb leadership readout.

Thanks,

Jonas Weber
Account Lead, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1-415-555-0142

From: Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Feb 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: QBR prep: ACME health snapshot + renewal risk & exec asks

Jonas — thanks for the clear summary. I added two technical risks in the Risk Register tab: 

- SDK adoption lag (owner: Grace Oconnor) — mitigation: schedule two week-long office hours + recorded walk-through with Acme ML infra; impact: Medium.
- Latency for long-context endpoints (owner: Infra Eng — Ben Carter) — mitigation: patch release with improved KV eviction & kernel tweaks; impact: High.

Quick notes below (will expand in the sheet):
- We should call out the business impact of the latency increase explicitly (engineers have paused full rollout of streaming features; this impacts projected usage and therefore renewal elasticity).
- Suggest we include a short timeline showing the patch ETA and a commitment to a targeted latency SLA improvement by end of March.

I'll drop a calendar invite for a 30-min triage sync Thursday.

—Grace
Grace Oconnor
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.com

Adding infra context — I uploaded a short technical note into the Drive folder (file: infra_root_cause_ACME_20280216.txt). TL;DR: the Sev2 was caused by a KV cache consistency bug that surfaces under specific mixed-load patterns. Patch is on a fast track; we have a staged rollout plan and a bench test showing 90% reduction in error window.

Draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) is attached here as a quick MAA placeholder; procurement is waiting on the MAA updates to move contract forward. DocuSign link included.

DocuSign (MAA v1.2): https://www.docusign.com/sign/MAA-ACME-2028
Drive note: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AcmeQBRPrep

Ben Carter
Head of Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Team + Acme — thanks for the quick turnaround. Consolidated update below (finalizing the one-pager for execs):

Executive attention items (two):
1) Reliability commitment & timeline: commit to a targeted 20ms average latency improvement for long-context endpoints by 2028-03-31; executive sponsor: Ben Carter.
2) Commercial cadence: accelerate MAA signature by providing a limited-term credit for the Jan incident and a 60-day joint success program to accelerate SDK adoption; executive sponsor: Jonas Weber.

Renewal risk register (top lines):
- Latency impact on adoption — Impact: High — Owner: Ben Carter — Mitigation: patch rollout + weekly perf reports to Acme (ETA: 2028-03-31).
- Slow SDK adoption — Impact: Medium — Owner: Grace Oconnor — Mitigation: office hours + co-developed onboarding playbook (ETA: 2028-03-15).
- Contract delay due to MAA redlines — Impact: Medium — Owner: Laura Bennett (legal) / Jonas Weber — Mitigation: provide MAA v1.2 with carve-outs and a short commercial credit (ETA: signature target 2028-03-10).

Next steps: 
- I will circulate the exec one-pager by Monday 20 Feb end-of-day.
- Ben: confirm patch rollout schedule in the Drive note and share weekly perf baseline.
- Grace: finalize onboarding plan and proposed office-hour schedule; copy Acme contacts.
- Laura/Aditya: confirm commercial credit wording and sign-off for MAA v1.2.

Sara / Michael (Acme) — appreciate the collaboration. Are you available for a 30-min readout next Wed 22 Feb at 10am PT? If not, propose alternatives.
